question.knowledge_point: Simplifying Expressions in Degrees Using the Sum and Difference Formulas
question.worked_solution:
First, we recall the difference formula for cosine:

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡(u-v)=\operatorname{cos}⁡u\operatorname{cos}⁡v+\operatorname{sin}⁡u\operatorname{sin}⁡v
$$

Applying the difference formula for cosine with $u=x$ and $v={210}^{∘},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(x-{210}^{∘}) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡{210}^{∘}+\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{sin}⁡{210}^{∘} \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡x\cdot (-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2})+\operatorname{sin}⁡x\cdot (-\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}(\sqrt{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡x+\operatorname{sin}⁡x).\end{aligned}
$$
